sections.title: Warm-up
sections.prompt: Say one thing that is done in your town every year, without saying who does it.
sections.lede: Say each line aloud once. This section is not scored.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: These are the three things you will be able to do by the end of the lesson.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: The passive moves the focus from the person acting to the action itself.

blocks.text: The passive is formed with werden plus the past participle: Die Rechnung wird morgen bezahlt. The thing that is affected becomes the subject, and the person doing it can be left out or added with von.

Use the passive when the action matters more than the actor, when the actor is unknown, or when you want to sound neutral and factual. In the past tense, werden becomes wurde: Die Rechnung wurde gestern bezahlt.

blocks.title: Active or passive?
blocks.text: Active: Der Techniker repariert das Gerät. Passive: Das Gerät wird repariert. The passive is shorter when the actor is irrelevant.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

rows: Das Brot wird jeden Morgen gebacken.
Das Buch wurde von Kafka geschrieben.

items: The past participle goes to the end of the clause.
Use von for a person or institution, and durch for a means or cause.
With a modal, werden stays in the infinitive at the end.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.lede: Listen once, then read the example aloud.

items.exampleEn: The invoice will be paid tomorrow.

items.example: Die Miete wird am ersten Tag bezahlt.
items.exampleEn: The rent is paid on the first day.

items.example: Das Buch wurde von einer Lehrerin geschrieben.
items.exampleEn: The book was written by a teacher.

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Notice how the pattern behaves in a complete sentence.

items.en: The invoice will be paid tomorrow.
The form must be filled in.
items.note: With a modal, werden goes to the end.

items.de: Der Kuchen wird von meiner Oma gebacken.
items.en: The cake is baked by my grandmother.
items.note: Von introduces the person doing the action.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

items.hint: The i is short and the r is soft: virt.

blocks.text: German official language often uses the passive to sound neutral: “Das Formular ist bis Freitag einzureichen.” This avoids blaming an individual and keeps rules impersonal.
In news, the passive lets reporters focus on events: “Die Straße wurde gesperrt.” It is not necessarily evasive; it simply puts the action first.

sections.title: Dialogue in context
sections.lede: Read the scene, then play it and follow the speakers.
sections.setting: A tenant calls the landlord about a broken heating system.

lines.speaker: Mieterin
lines.de: Die Heizung ist kaputt. Wann wird sie repariert?
lines.en: The heating is broken. When will it be repaired?

lines.speaker: Vermieter
lines.de: Ein Techniker wird morgen früh geschickt.
lines.en: A technician will be sent tomorrow morning.

lines.speaker: Mieterin
lines.en: Has the problem already been reported?

lines.speaker: Vermieter
lines.de: Ja, die Meldung wurde gestern gemacht.
lines.en: Yes, the report was made yesterday.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Forming the passive
sections.lede: Werden carries the tense; the past participle carries the meaning.

blocks.text: The agent is optional. Add von + dative for a person: von der Lehrerin. Use durch for a means: durch den Sturm.

sections.tip: Check the participle first, then conjugate werden to match the subject and tense.

sections.title: Choose the right answer
sections.lede: Choose the answer that fits the sentence or the rule.

exercises.explanation: Present passive with a singular subject uses wird.
The past passive of a singular subject uses wurde.
With a modal, werden stays in the infinitive at the end.

options: Der Techniker hat das Gerät repariert.
exercises.explanation: Werden plus past participle marks the passive.

sections.title: Complete the sentence
sections.lede: Type the missing word or ending. Spelling counts.

exercises.explanation: The modal construction ends with werden.
Von introduces the person who performed the action.

sections.title: Build the sentence
sections.lede: Click the words in the order that makes a correct German sentence.

exercises.prompt: Build: “The invoice will be paid tomorrow.”
exercises.explanation: Wird is the conjugated auxiliary; bezahlt closes the sentence.
Wurde marks the past passive and the participle is final.

exercises.prompt: Build: “The form must be filled in.”
exercises.explanation: The modal is second, the participle follows, and werden closes the sentence.

exercises.prompt: Build: “The cake is baked by my grandmother.”
exercises.answer: Der Kuchen wird von meiner Oma gebacken.
exercises.explanation: Von plus dative names the agent before the final participle.

sections.title: Listening
sections.lede: Listen twice before you look at the transcript.
sections.speaker: Nachrichten im Radio

script.speaker: Sprecher
script.de: Die neue Brücke wurde am Montag eröffnet.
script.en: The new bridge was opened on Monday.

script.speaker: Sprecher
script.de: Wegen des Sturms wurden mehrere Straßen gesperrt.
script.en: Because of the storm, several roads were closed.

script.speaker: Sprecher
script.de: Die Reparaturen werden voraussichtlich zwei Wochen dauern.
script.en: The repairs are expected to take two weeks.

script.speaker: Sprecher
script.en: Further information will be published tomorrow.

questions.explanation: The first line says the new bridge was opened on Monday.

questions.prompt: How long will the repairs take?
questions.explanation: The reporter says the repairs will probably take two weeks.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Describe three things that happen in your town without saying who does them. Use the passive.

model.de: Jeden Samstag wird der Markt geöffnet. Die Straßen werden am Morgen gereinigt. Im Sommer werden viele Feste gefeiert.
model.en: Every Saturday the market is opened. The streets are cleaned in the morning. In summer many festivals are celebrated.

tips: Start with the thing affected, then use werden + participle.
Keep the participle at the end of the clause.
Use wurde for a completed past event.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.why: The passive needs the past participle bezahlt.
Do not combine wurde with worden in the simple past passive.
After a modal, the passive auxiliary stays in the infinitive.
